Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

ūtor

ūtor, ūtī, ūsus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative; with familiāriter, of friendship

be on close terms with, associate with (a person); have, enjoy (health, good weather, a friendship, an office); wear regularly

In this lexicon

  • associate

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.3.1: multōs annōs ūtor valdē familiāriter; Cic. Att. 16.5.3: Luccejus, quī multum ūtitur Brūtō (Lewis & Short)

  • enjoy

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BC 3.49.2: ūtī autem ipsōs valētūdine nōn bonā; Traupman 61, 63, 310

  • wear

    also used · classical · Traupman 405

Examples

  • A. Trebōniō, quī in tuā prōvinciā magna negōtia et ampla et expedīta habet, multōs annōs ūtor valdē familiāriter

    Aulus Trebonius, who has large and well-run business interests in your province, has been a close friend of mine for many yearsCic. Fam. 1.3.1

    In the entry for associate

  • Mīrum est, nam valētūdine bonā ūteris.

    That’s strange, since you enjoy good health.Traupman 61

    In the entry for enjoy

  • suum cuique per mē ūtī atque fruī licet

    as far as I am concerned, everyone may have and enjoy what is hisGell. 13.24.1

    In the entry for enjoy
